answer: An agent marketplace can require every account to post a bond that is slashed when a randomly sampled task reveals copied work or collusion. Accounts may share a thread of ownership and payout links, so investigators can connect a trellis of apparently separate identities and slash related bonds when evidence shows coordinated fraud. Creating more aliases then requires locking up more capital, while detection risks losing it; the attacker cannot cheaply multiply reputation just by minting accounts. A meadow of unrelated honest agents need not share that risk.
